evidence: Caes. BC 2.38: Numidae enim quādam barbarā cōnsuētūdine nūllīs ōrdinibus passim cōnsēderant
Ov. F. 3.525–526: plēbs venit ac viridēs passim disjecta per herbās pōtat
terms.comment: Of things or people spread about in no order; it stretches to “all over the place” (see everywhere).

terms.gloss: here … there, in one place … in another
evidence: Liv. 26.45: ut alibī umbilīcō tenus aqua esset, alibī genua vix superāret

terms.gloss: this way and that, to and fro (of movement)
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.9.2: nē forte aut absim cum veniet aut cursem hūc illūc viā dēterrimā
Ter. Eun. 105: plēnus rīmārum sum, hāc atque illāc perfluō
terms.comment: hūc illūc of going to and fro; hāc atque illāc, Terence’s slave of a secret leaking out on every side.

phrases.latin: Frāga passim in silvā crēscunt; quaerāmus ea.
phrases.english: Wild strawberries grow here and there in the wood; let’s look for them.

phrases.latin: Alibī lutum est, alibī siccum; cavē quō pedem pōnās.
phrases.english: Here it’s muddy, there it’s dry; watch where you put your foot.

phrases.latin: adeō nūdāverat vada ut alibī umbilīcō tenus aqua esset, alibī genua vix superāret
phrases.english: had so laid bare the shallows that in places the water came up to the waist, in others barely above the knee

phrases.latin: nē forte aut absim cum veniet aut cursem hūc illūc viā dēterrimā
phrases.english: so as not to be away when he comes, or dashing here and there on a dreadful road

sources: Lewis & Short: passim · Lewis & Short: alibi · Lewis & Short: huc
